exercise: Exercise 2: eigenvalues and eigenvectors of B = [[4,1],[2,3]], diagonalizable?
secret: The eigenvalues are 5 and 2 (characteristic polynomial λ² − 7λ + 10). Eigenvectors: (1,1) for 5 and (1,−2) for 2. B is diagonalizable (two distinct eigenvalues).

steps.text: You skipped why the determinant has to be zero. Why does det(B − λI) = 0 give the eigenvalues?
OK: λ² − 7λ + 10 = 0, so λ = 5 and λ = 2.

exercise: Q4: for each department, the average salary of employees hired after 2020, only departments with at least 5 such employees, ordered by average.
secret: SELECT dept, AVG(salary) AS avg_sal FROM Employee WHERE hire_date > '2020-12-31' GROUP BY dept HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ORDER BY avg_sal;

steps.first_error: An aggregate (COUNT) cannot be used in WHERE; the group condition belongs in HAVING after GROUP BY. (ORDER BY is also missing.)

steps.text: You didn't explain the order in which SQL evaluates WHERE, GROUP BY and HAVING.
SELECT dept, AVG(salary) AS avg_sal FROM Employee WHERE hire_date > '2020-12-31' GROUP BY dept HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5 ORDER BY avg_sal;

title: SQL grouping

exercise: Problem 1: conducting sphere of radius R with charge Q. E(r) everywhere with Gauss's law, and V(r).
secret: E = 0 for r < R; E = Q/(4πε₀ r²) radially for r > R. V = Q/(4πε₀ R) for r ≤ R and Q/(4πε₀ r) for r ≥ R.
